name: Android SQLite query built by string concatenation (rawQuery/execSQL)
attack_scenario: A malicious value (e.g. name = ' OR '1'='1' --) closes the string literal and appends attacker SQL, turning a single-row SQLite lookup into an arbitrary read/write or auth bypass on the on-device database.
negative_test_hint: submit name = "' OR '1'='1' -- " and assert rawQuery returns a single row or errors, not the whole table

exemplar.noncompliant: val c = db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'", null)
exemplar.compliant: val c = db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", arrayOf(name))
exemplar.explanation: SQLiteDatabase.rawQuery/execSQL take raw SQL, so a concatenated or Kotlin-interpolated value is parsed as SQL and can inject clauses. Pass the value as a ? placeholder with the selectionArgs array (arrayOf(name)); the driver binds it as data that can never be reinterpreted as SQL.
